implementation_notes: The JVM realization is the same persistence context Java uses: Hibernate tracks entity changes in memory and writes in a write-behind fashion at flush/commit time, and Kotlin property accessors funnel through the identical dirty checking, so no Kotlin-specific buffer exists. Keep the EntityManager request-scoped, drive the boundary with @Transactional or em.flush(), and treat nullable/data-class ergonomics as sugar over the same rules. What replaces the classic structure: the JPA persistence context.
pitfalls: Data-class copy() creates a detached instance: only mutations on the managed entity are tracked, so save the copy or mutate in place.
Property access outside the transaction touches a detached entity; Hibernate sessions are not thread-safe and coroutine dispatchers do not change that.
A suspend function that calls blocking JPA on the wrong dispatcher starves the pool, and @Transactional is thread-bound unless the reactive transaction manager is configured.

variants.name: Coroutine Channel + flush worker
variants.idiom_name: kotlinx.coroutines Channel with a drain-and-flush worker
variants.implementation_notes: Without a JPA context (Exposed, raw JDBC, or cross-request batching), Kotlin's Channel plus a launched worker is the idiomatic queue: a bounded Channel<Change> gives suspending back-pressure instead of a hand-written watermark, and a single consumer coroutine drains up to a batch size and executes one transaction per batch, optionally woken by delay() for the time trigger. The producer/consumer pair replaces the classic dirty-set-plus-flush-thread structure; the coroutine version is justified when the application is already structured around structured concurrency.
pitfalls: A rendezvous (capacity 0) channel suspends every stage() until the flusher is ready; choose BUFFERED, CONFLATED, or an explicit capacity deliberately.
A cancelled worker coroutine abandons the in-flight batch unless the final flush runs in NonCancellable before shutdown.
Channel.send from many producers still needs idempotent flush semantics: a crash between commit and batch.clear() replays the batch.
